description: Reference for EAGLE 9.6 data: the predefined board and schematic layers with their numbers, names and manufacturing meaning (verified against the LAYER help page, the manual and the layer tables of 9.3+ example files), user-defined layers, the file types EAGLE reads and writes (drawings, design blocks, scripts, ULPs, CAM jobs, design rules, autorouter, project, settings, backups, device definitions, SPICE) and the main elements of the XML format described by eagle.dtd.

tools.name: Layer 1 Top
tools.description: The top (component side) copper layer for tracks, polygons and SMDs of parts placed on top. Together with 17 Pads and 18 Vias it forms the top copper film, and in the default two-layer setup (1*16) it is connected to layer 16 by through vias.
tools.usage: LAYER 1 | LAYER TOP | CHANGE LAYER TOP   (ULP constant LAYER_TOP)
tools.notes: Signal layers can only be used if they appear in the layer setup of the design rules.

tools.name: Layers 2-15 Route2 ... Route15
tools.description: The fourteen inner signal layers, used like Top and Bottom for tracks and polygons (e.g. ground and supply planes). They must be enabled in Design Rules > Layers > Setup; a typical 4-layer setup (1*2+15*16) uses Route2 and Route15, a 6-layer setup Route2, Route3, Route14 and Route15.
tools.usage: LAYER 2 ... LAYER 15 | LAYER Route2
tools.notes: Inner layers are exported together with 17 Pads and 18 Vias. Pads and vias are always round in inner layers, sized by the annular ring rules.

tools.name: Layer 16 Bottom
tools.description: The bottom (solder side) copper layer. Mirrored parts place their SMDs here, and single-sided boards use only this layer (setup '16').
tools.usage: LAYER 16 | LAYER BOTTOM   (ULP constant LAYER_BOTTOM)
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oboard.sol board.brd 16 17 18

tools.name: Layers 17 Pads / 18 Vias
tools.description: Generated layers that hold through-hole pads (17) and vias (18); they are combined with each signal layer when copper films are produced. Nothing should be drawn into them manually - the DRC reports this as Layer Abuse.
tools.usage: Included automatically by PAD and VIA; add 17 18 to every copper output
tools.example: "layers": [16, 17, 18]    # bottom copper Gerber item
tools.notes: If the colour of layers 17/18 is set to 0 (background), pads and vias are shown in the colour and shape of each visible signal layer, which reveals per-layer shapes. With blind/buried vias, a signal layer plus 18 outputs only the vias on that layer; 18 alone outputs all vias.

tools.name: Layer 19 Unrouted
tools.description: Holds the airwires (rubber bands) of connections not yet routed. RATSNEST recalculates them, the DRC lists remaining ones as Airwire errors, and signal names on pads and traces are drawn in this layer's colour.
tools.usage: DISPLAY 19 | RATSNEST;
tools.example:
RATSNEST;          # optimise airwires and calculate polygons
RATSNEST ! GND;    # hide the GND airwires

tools.name: Layer 20 Dimension
tools.description: Board outline and other dimension contours. A single closed, non-self-intersecting shape is recognised as the board shape and inner closed shapes as cutouts; the lines bound the autorouter, copper keeps the Copper/Dimension distance to them, and HOLEs create circles of their diameter here. Since 9.6 SPLINE curves can be drawn, restricted to this layer.
tools.usage: CHANGE LAYER DIMENSION | LAYER 20   (ULP constant LAYER_DIMENSION)
tools.notes: Ask the manufacturer whether the outline should be a separate file or merged into silkscreen; JSON CAM jobs export it via a Profile item with board_outline.

tools.name: Layers 21 tPlace / 22 bPlace
tools.description: Silkscreen (component print) for the top and bottom side, normally drawn as footprint outlines in the library. Silkscreen outputs combine them with the name layers (21 + 25 top, 22 + 26 bottom), and the DRC can flag silkscreen overlapping solder-stop openings.
tools.usage: LAYER 21 | LAYER tPlace   (ULP LAYER_TPLACE / LAYER_BPLACE)
tools.example:
"layers": [21, 25]  -> silkscreen_top.gbr
eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oboard.plc board.brd 20 21 25
tools.notes: Mirroring a part moves its top-layer objects to the matching bottom layer (t*/b* pairs).

tools.name: Layers 23 tOrigins / 24 bOrigins
tools.description: Automatically generated origin marks of the elements placed on the top and bottom side. Displaying them shows where each element's origin lies, i.e. the point stored as the element's x/y position in the board file.
tools.usage: DISPLAY 23 24
tools.example: DISPLAY = 'Preset_Top' None 1 17 18 19 20 21 23 25 39 41 51;   # shipped eagle.scr shows tOrigins in the top preset

tools.name: Layers 25 tNames / 26 bNames
tools.description: Service print of component names: the >NAME placeholder texts of footprints are placed here and show the actual part name (R1, U3 ...). They are usually output together with tPlace/bPlace on the silkscreen.
tools.usage: TEXT '>NAME' in the footprint on layer 25; SMASH to move it in the board
tools.example: Footprint editor: CHANGE LAYER tNames; TEXT '>NAME' (0 1.5);

tools.name: Layers 27 tValues / 28 bValues
tools.description: Component values: the >VALUE placeholder texts of footprints show the part value (10k, 100n ...). They are usually not printed on the silkscreen but are useful for assembly drawings.
tools.usage: TEXT '>VALUE' in the footprint on layer 27
tools.example: Footprint editor: CHANGE LAYER tValues; TEXT '>VALUE' (0 -1.5);
tools.notes: Since 8.5 the DRC can be told to omit tValues/bValues from its checks.

tools.name: Layers 29 tStop / 30 bStop
tools.description: Solder stop mask. Openings for SMDs, pads and vias (above the via Limit) are generated automatically from the Masks design rules; additional openings can be drawn, and pads/SMDs with STOP off in the library get none. The films are exported as solder mask files.
tools.usage: Automatic; extra shapes on LAYER 29/30   (Gerber: [29] top, [30] bottom)
tools.example: "config": {"file_function": "Soldermask", "layer_type": "top", "index": 1}, "layers": [29]
tools.notes: The DRC Stop Mask check compares these layers with the silkscreen layers.

tools.name: Layers 31 tCream / 32 bCream
tools.description: Solder cream (paste) masks for stencils, generated for SMDs only according to the Masks cream rules. Paste Gerbers of the CAM Processor leave out parts that are not populated in the current assembly variant.
tools.usage: Automatic for SMDs (CREAM flag); Gerber items with layers [31] / [32]
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oboard.crc board.brd 31

tools.name: Layers 33 tFinish / 34 bFinish
tools.description: Finish layers for areas that receive a special surface finish, such as gold coating, on the top and bottom side. The manual's file list exports them as %N.fic and %N.fis.
tools.usage: LAYER 33 | LAYER tFinish
tools.example: eaglecon -X -dGERBER_RS274X -oboard.fic board.brd 33

tools.name: Layers 35 tGlue / 36 bGlue
tools.description: Glue mask for SMDs that must be glued before soldering, for the top and bottom side. gluemark.ulp uses circles drawn on tGlue in the footprints (or a default point) to generate glue points, and glueout.ulp exports dispenser data.
tools.usage: CIRCLE on LAYER 35 in footprints; Gerber output %N.glc / %N.gls
tools.example:
RUN gluemark;
RUN glueout;

tools.name: Layers 37 tTest / 38 bTest
tools.description: Test and adjustment information for the top and bottom side (e.g. test point marks). The pair mirrors like all t/b layers and may also be used for custom purposes.
tools.usage: LAYER 37 | LAYER tTest
tools.example: CHANGE LAYER tTest; CIRCLE 0 (25 30) (25.5 30);   # mark a test point

tools.name: Layers 39 tKeepout / 40 bKeepout
tools.description: Keepout areas for components on the top and bottom side, normally drawn in footprints. The DRC reports overlapping keepouts as Keepout errors, but only when these layers are displayed.
tools.usage: RECT/CIRCLE/POLYGON on LAYER 39 in footprints; DISPLAY 39 40 before DRC
tools.example: Footprint: CHANGE LAYER tKeepout; RECT (-2 -1.5) (2 1.5);

tools.name: Layers 41 tRestrict / 42 bRestrict / 43 vRestrict
tools.description: Restricted areas: 41 and 42 forbid copper on the top and bottom side, 43 forbids vias. The autorouter treats them as obstacles, and the DRC (Misc > Check restrict) reports copper inside tRestrict/bRestrict areas.
tools.usage: RECT, CIRCLE or POLYGON on LAYER 41/42/43 (board or footprint)
tools.example:
CHANGE LAYER vRestrict;
RECT (10 10) (25 20);   # no vias under the crystal
tools.notes: Copper and restrict objects in the same footprint are not checked against each other; cutout polygons as restrict areas are not checked by the DRC.

tools.name: Layers 44 Drills / 45 Holes
tools.description: 44 Drills holds the conducting (plated) holes of pads and vias, 45 Holes the non-conducting holes placed with HOLE. Drill outputs use 44 and 45 together or separately (plated vs. non-plated), and drill plans show a symbol per diameter in these layers as configured in Options > Set > Drill.
tools.usage: Generated by PAD/VIA (44) and HOLE (45); drill output layers 44 45
tools.example:
eaglecon -X -dEXCELLON -oboard.drd board.brd 44 45
HOLE 3.2 (5 5);   # mounting hole in layer 45
tools.notes: The shipped drillegend-stack.ulp draws a drill legend with the drill symbols into layer 144 (default).

tools.name: Layer 46 Milling
tools.description: Milling contours for slots, cut-outs and board edges that must be milled. Closed shapes on this layer are treated as board cutouts, and the manual's file list exports it as plated milling contours (%N.mill).
tools.usage: LINE on LAYER 46 (in the board or in footprints for slotted holes)
tools.example:
CHANGE LAYER MILLING;
LINE 0 (20 10) (35 10) (35 14) (20 14) (20 10);   # rectangular cut-out
tools.notes: Ask the board house which layer they expect milling data in; the shipped gerb274x-mill-drill.cam outputs it as %N.mil.

tools.name: Layers 47 Measures / 48 Document / 49 Reference
tools.description: Documentation layers: 47 Measures for measurements, 48 Document for general documentation and 49 Reference for reference marks. The manual recommends fiducials or crop marks in layer 49 (e.g. from marks.lbr), output together with the signal layers so that films can be aligned.
tools.usage: LAYER 47 | LAYER 48 | LAYER 49
tools.example:
CHANGE LAYER Document;
TEXT 'Rev B - 2026-09-27' (0 -5);

tools.name: Layers 51 tDocu / 52 bDocu
tools.description: Part documentation for the top and bottom side, a more detailed outline of the component than the silkscreen (for assembly drawings). They are included in the shipped board display presets but usually not in fabrication outputs.
tools.usage: LINE/TEXT on LAYER 51 in footprints
tools.example:
DISPLAY NONE 20 21 25 51;
PRINT FILE %N_assembly_top.pdf;   # top assembly drawing

tools.name: Layers 88 SimResults / 89 SimProbes / 99 SpiceOrder
tools.description: Schematic layers used by the built-in SPICE simulator (ngspice) in files from 9.3 on. 88 SimResults carries operating-point result labels (switched with SIMOPTOGGLE), 89 SimProbes carries the probes placed with VPROBE/VPPROBE, and 99 SpiceOrder carries 'SpiceOrder n' texts in symbols that define the pin order for the SPICE model.
tools.usage: Created automatically in schematics/libraries; <probe ... layer="89"/>, <text layer="99">SpiceOrder 1</text>
tools.example:
<layer number="88" name="SimResults" color="9" fill="1" visible="yes" active="yes"/>
<layer number="89" name="SimProbes" color="9" fill="1" visible="yes" active="yes"/>
<layer number="99" name="SpiceOrder" color="5" fill="1" visible="yes" active="yes"/>
tools.notes: The 9.6 help page of LAYER lists these as 100 SimOp and 101 SimProbes, but the shipped 9.3+ example schematics and design blocks use 88/89 and 99, with 100 and 101 free for user layers.

tools.name: Layer 90 Modules
tools.description: Schematic layer in which module instances and their ports are drawn automatically in hierarchical designs. Modules are created with MODULE, their connection points defined with PORT, and nets attach to them through port references.
tools.usage: Automatic when placing module instances
tools.example: <layer number="90" name="Modules" color="5" fill="1" visible="yes" active="yes"/>

tools.name: Layers 91 Nets / 92 Busses
tools.description: Schematic layers for net wires (drawn with NET) and bus lines (drawn with BUS). The XML stores net segments as <wire ... layer="91"/> inside <net><segment>.
tools.usage: NET / BUS draw automatically into 91 / 92
tools.example: <net name="VCAP1" class="0"><segment><wire x1="43.18" y1="40.64" x2="43.18" y2="27.94" width="0.1524" layer="91"/><pinref part="R1" gate="G$1" pin="2"/></segment></net>

tools.name: Layers 93 Pins / 94 Symbols
tools.description: Symbol layers: 93 Pins holds the connection points of symbol pins with their additional information, and 94 Symbols holds the drawn shape of the component symbol. Both are drawn in the library's symbol editor and appear with every placed instance in the schematic.
tools.usage: PIN places on 93; LINE/ARC/RECT for the symbol body on 94

tools.name: Layers 95 Names / 96 Values
tools.description: Schematic layers for the >NAME and >VALUE placeholder texts of symbols, which display the actual part name and value. Net labels are commonly placed on 95 as well, and SMASH detaches the texts so that they can be moved individually.
tools.usage: TEXT '>NAME' on 95 and '>VALUE' on 96 in the symbol
tools.example: Symbol editor: CHANGE LAYER Names; TEXT '>NAME' (-5.08 6.35); CHANGE LAYER Values; TEXT '>VALUE' (-5.08 -7.62);

tools.name: Layers 97 Info / 98 Guide
tools.description: 97 Info carries additional information and hints in schematics and symbols. 98 Guide carries guide lines that help to align symbols.
tools.usage: LAYER 97 | LAYER 98
tools.example: CHANGE LAYER Info; TEXT 'Place C5 close to U2 pin 7' (50 20);

tools.name: User-defined layers and custom top/bottom pairs
tools.description: Own layers should use numbers above 100 (LAYER_USER = 100), because lower numbers may get special meanings; LAYER number name creates or renames one, and layers used in a footprint are added to the board automatically when it is placed. Additional top/bottom pairs that swap when mirrored can be created as 53/54, 55/56, 57/58 and 59/60. LAYER -number deletes an empty layer, and '??' suppresses errors in scripts.
tools.usage: LAYER number name; | LAYER -number; | LAYER ?? -number;
tools.notes: Predefined layers can be renamed but keep their function. Layer presets (DISPLAY = 'name' layers) are defined in eagle.scr or through the DISPLAY dialog (up to 9 user presets per editor type).

tools.name: .sch
tools.description: Schematic file: an XML document (root <eagle>, <drawing> with <schematic>) holding the used libraries, global attributes, assembly variants, net classes, modules, parts and sheets with instances, busses and nets. A board with the same name in the same directory forms the consistent pair used for forward & back annotation.
tools.usage: EDIT name.sch; | eagle name.sch | ULP schematic(S) { ... }
tools.example:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE eagle SYSTEM "eagle.dtd">
<eagle version="9.6.0">
<drawing> <settings>...</settings> <grid .../> <layers>...</layers>
<schematic xreflabel="%F%N/%S.%C%R" xrefpart="/%S.%C%R"> ... </schematic>
</drawing>
</eagle>
tools.notes: Simulation settings are kept next to it in <name>.sch.simcfg; backups are .s#1-.s#9 and .s##.

tools.name: .brd
tools.description: Board file: XML with <board> holding plain objects, used libraries, attributes, variants, net classes, design rules, autorouter parameters, elements (placed footprints) and signals with their wires, vias, polygons and pad references. A file name without extension on the command line is assumed to be .brd, which is also what eaglecon -X reads.
tools.usage: EDIT name.brd; | eaglecon -X ... name.brd | ULP board(B) { ... }
tools.example:
<board>
<plain> <wire x1="0" y1="0" x2="100" y2="0" width="0" layer="20"/> ... </plain>
<designrules name="default"> <param name="layerSetup" value="(1*16)"/> ... </designrules>
<elements> <element name="R1" library="rcl" package="R0603" value="10k" x="10" y="5"/> </elements>
<signals> <signal name="GND" class="1"> <contactref element="R1" pad="2"/> </signal> </signals>
</board>

tools.name: .lbr
tools.description: Library file: XML with <library> containing packages (footprints), 3D packages, symbols and devicesets (gates, devices with connects, technologies and attributes, optional SPICE mapping). Boards and schematics embed copies of the libraries they use, which is why an old design keeps working without the original .lbr.
tools.usage: OPEN name.lbr; (edit) | USE name.lbr; (place parts) | ULP library(L) { ... }
tools.example:
<library>
<packages> <package name="R0603"> <smd name="1" x="-0.75" y="0" dx="0.9" dy="1" layer="1"/> ... </package> </packages>
<symbols> <symbol name="R"> <pin name="1" x="-5.08" y="0" length="short" direction="pas"/> ... </symbol> </symbols>
<devicesets> <deviceset name="R" prefix="R" uservalue="yes"> ... </deviceset> </devicesets>
</library>
tools.notes: Managed libraries carry urn attributes (urn:adsk.eagle:<type>:<id>/<version>). Backups are .l#1-.l#9 and .l##.

tools.name: .dbl
tools.description: Design block: a reusable circuit fragment stored as <eagle><designblock> with a description, attributes and one <drawing> containing a schematic, optionally followed by a second <drawing> with the matching board. Shipped examples (voltage regulators, transistor stages, Adafruit breakouts ...) are in examples\design blocks.
tools.usage: EDIT name.dbl (preview) | EDIT name.dbl; (load into the editors) | Control Panel > Design Blocks > Add to Schematic
tools.example:
<eagle version="9.3.2">
<designblock>
<description>Current mirror ...</description>
<attributes> ... </attributes>
<drawing> ... <schematic> ... </schematic> </drawing>
</designblock>
</eagle>
tools.notes: The <designblock> wrapper is not declared in the shipped eagle.dtd. Backups use .d#n and .d##.

tools.name: .scr
tools.description: Script file: plain text with editor commands in the normal command syntax, one or more per line; lines starting with '#' are comments and a '\' at the end of a line keeps the next line's first word from being read as a command. SCRIPT runs it (adding .scr if no extension is given), EXPORT can write scripts from drawings, and ULPs can hand scripts back via exit().
tools.usage: SCRIPT name[.scr]; | drop on an editor | Control Panel > Execute in ...
tools.notes: Use '.' as decimal separator. Shipped examples include eagle.scr, default-assign.scr, defaultcolors.scr, menu.scr and mylayers.scr.

tools.name: .ulp
tools.description: User Language program source: a C-like text file executed by RUN, which reads the loaded board, schematic or library, can write files with output(), build dialogs and return commands to the editor with exit(). The #usage directive supplies the description shown in the Control Panel.
tools.usage: RUN name[.ulp] [arguments]; | drop on an editor | Control Panel > Run in ...

tools.name: .cam
tools.description: CAM Processor job. Since 8.6 it is JSON (type 'EAGLE CAM job' with gerber, drill, assembly and drawing sections); older jobs are INI-style text with a [CAM Processor Job] header and [Sec_n] sections naming an eagle.def device, output file and layers. Both kinds can be processed by the CAM Processor and by eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB.
tools.usage: CAM Processor > Load job file | eaglecon -X -dCAMJOB -j<job.cam> -o<dir> board.brd
tools.example:
{ "type": "EAGLE CAM job", "version": "9.2.0", "units": "metric", "output_type": "directory", "outputs": [ ... ] }

[CAM Processor Job]
Section=Sec_1
[Sec_1]
Device="EXCELLON"
Output="%N.drd"
Layers=" 44 45"
tools.notes: Shipped jobs: examples\cam\examples (example_N_layer.cam, Third Party, Legacy).

tools.name: .dru
tools.description: Design rules file: plain text with one 'key = value' line per parameter, language-specific description[en]/description[de] lines (HTML), the layerSetup string and the md*, ms*, rv*, rl*, ps*, sr*, sl*, ml*, mv*, dp* and check* parameters of the Design Rules tabs. Inside a board the same parameters are stored as <designrules name="..."><param name="..." value="..."/></designrules>.
tools.usage: DRC LOAD|SAVE|MERGE file.dru; | Design Rules > File > Load... / Save as...
tools.example: description[en] = Company 2 layer, 6 mil layerSetup = (1*16) mdWireWire = 6mil msWidth = 6mil msDrill = 0.3mm rvViaOuter = 0.250000 mlMinStopFrame = 2mil checkFont = 1
tools.notes: Values carry units (mil, mm); ratios are fractions (0.25 = 25 %). maxErrors is still accepted but ignored.

tools.name: .ctl / .pro (autorouter files)
tools.description: Autorouter control files (.ctl) are INI-like text with a [Default] section and further passes holding parameters such as RoutingGrid, via shape, preferred direction per layer (PrefDir.1 ... PrefDir.16) and cost factors; AUTO LOAD/SAVE reads and writes them, and the board stores the same data as <autorouter><pass><param/></pass></autorouter>. Each autorouter run writes a protocol file name.pro; the manual's file table additionally lists autorouter job files (.job) and a board backup made after autorouting (.b$$).
tools.usage: AUTO LOAD name.ctl; | AUTO SAVE name.ctl;
tools.example:
; EAGLE Autorouter Control File
[Default]
  RoutingGrid     = 25mil
  tpViaShape      = Round
  PrefDir.1       = |
  PrefDir.16      = -
  Active          = 1
tools.notes: Shipped examples: projects\examples\singlesided\singlesided_h.ctl / singlesided_v.ctl and tutorial\hexapodu.ctl.

tools.name: eagle.epf
tools.description: Project file in every project folder. It records the libraries in use, the open editor windows with their positions and contents, and CHANGE presets plus the contents of the Width, Diameter and Size menus. It is written on project close or exit (if automatic saving is on) and by File > Save all.
tools.usage: Created with New Project; eagle path\eagle.epf opens it; ULP constant eagle_epf
tools.example: eagle D:\Work\PowerSupply\eagle.epf
tools.notes: Project files from before 6.0 store dimensions differently; EAGLE asks before overwriting a file from another version.

tools.name: Backup files (.b#n, .s#n, .l#n, .d#n, .b##, .s##, .l##, .d##)
tools.description: Backups of boards (b), schematics (s), libraries (l) and design blocks (d). WRITE keeps up to nine numbered generations .x#1 (newest) to .x#9, and the auto-backup timer writes a safety copy .x## that disappears after the next successful save. Both are complete drawing files that can be renamed back to their normal extension.
tools.usage: Automatic; configure in Control Panel > Options > Backup
tools.example:
copy demo2.b#1 demo2_previous.brd
del *.?#?
tools.notes: Linux versions create and recognise only lower-case file extensions.

tools.name: eaglerc
tools.description: The user settings file with SET options, ASSIGN key assignments, user-interface settings, directories, custom context-menu entries, predefined busses and the currently loaded project. In 9.x it is version-specific: on Windows C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Eagle\settings\<X.Y.Z>\eaglerc (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Eagle/settings/<X.Y.Z>/eaglerc, Linux ~/.local/share/Eagle/settings/<X.Y.Z>/eaglerc).
tools.usage: Written by EAGLE; select another file with -U<file>, or none with -U-; change hidden parameters with SET Parameter.Name value
tools.example:
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Eagle\settings\9.6.0\eaglerc
eagle -UC:/Settings/eaglerc5.usr
tools.notes: Older Windows versions called it eaglerc.usr (a new installation backs it up as eaglerc.usr.sav, .eaglerc.sav on Linux/macOS). The manual advises not to edit these files by hand.

tools.name: eagle.def (device definitions)
tools.description: Text file in the bin folder that defines the legacy output devices of the CAM Processor and command line. Each device is a [NAME] section with a Type (PenPlotter, PhotoPlotter, DrillStation, Generic, Calcomp, CalcompE) and parameters; '@NAME' inherits another section, strings are in double quotes with C-like escapes, '\' at line end continues a string and ';' starts a comment.
tools.usage: C:\Program Files\EAGLE 9.6.0\bin\eagle.def   (list: eaglecon -d?)
tools.example:
[GERBERAUTO]

@GERBER
Long          = "Gerber photoplotter with automatic aperture wheel generation"
Wheel         = "" ; avoids message!
AutoAperture  = "D%d" ; (Aperture number)
FirstAperture = 10
Units         = Inch

tools.name: .whl / .drl
tools.description: Plain-text tables for legacy devices: an aperture wheel (.whl) maps D-codes to aperture type and size for RS-274D photoplotters, and a drill rack (.drl) maps tool numbers to drill diameters for drill stations without automatic tables. drillcfg.ulp generates a rack for the current board.
tools.usage: -W<file.whl> / Wheel field;  -R<file.drl> / Rack field
tools.notes: The legacy CAM example folder ships glaser.whl for the GLASER photoplotter.

tools.name: .mdl / .sch.simcfg (SPICE)
tools.description: Files of the built-in ngspice simulation. .mdl files contain SPICE models (shipped examples such as OPAMP.mdl, QNPN.mdl and NFET.mdl in examples\spice; the user model folder is set in Options > Directories). <schematic>.sch.simcfg is a JSON file next to the schematic in which the SIM dialog automatically stores its analysis settings and solver options.
tools.usage: SIM (dialog) loads/saves <name>.sch.simcfg automatically; SPICE model names without .mdl in the SIM/ADDMODEL settings

tools.name: <eagle> / <drawing> (XML document structure)
tools.description: Every EAGLE XML file has the root <eagle version="..."> with optional <compatibility> notes and exactly one <drawing>. The drawing contains optional <settings> (always vector font, vertical text direction), <grid> (distance, unit, style, multiple, display and the alternate grid), optional <filters> (saved Design Manager filters), the <layers> list and then one of <library>, <schematic> or <board>.
tools.usage:
<!ELEMENT eagle (compatibility?, drawing, compatibility?)>
<!ELEMENT drawing (settings?, grid?, filters?, layers, (library | schematic | board))>
tools.example:
<eagle version="9.2.0">
<drawing>
<settings><setting alwaysvectorfont="no"/><setting verticaltext="up"/></settings>
<grid distance="0.1" unitdist="inch" unit="inch" style="lines" multiple="1" display="no" altdistance="0.01" altunitdist="inch" altunit="inch"/>
<layers><layer number="1" name="Top" color="4" fill="1" visible="yes" active="yes"/> ...</layers>
<board> ... </board>
</drawing>
</eagle>
tools.notes: Coordinates and dimensions are in millimetres; rotations are strings like R90, MR180 or SR45 (S = spin). The DTD is in the installation's doc folder and is published under CC BY-ND 3.0 for implementers of readers and writers.

tools.name: <library> (XML)
tools.description: Library content, used as the drawing content of .lbr files and embedded in <libraries> of boards and schematics. It holds <packages>/<package> (footprint primitives, pads and SMDs), <packages3d>/<package3d>, <symbols>/<symbol> (graphics and <pin>s) and <devicesets>/<deviceset>. A deviceset contains <gates>/<gate>, <devices>/<device> (package, <connects>/<connect gate pin pad route>, <package3dinstances>, <technologies>/<technology> with <attribute>s) and an optional <spice> pin mapping and model.
tools.usage: <!ELEMENT library (description?, packages?, packages3d?, symbols?, devicesets?)>
tools.example:
<deviceset name="R" prefix="R" uservalue="yes">
<gates><gate name="G$1" symbol="R" x="0" y="0"/></gates>
<devices><device name="0603" package="R0603">
<connects><connect gate="G$1" pin="1" pad="1"/><connect gate="G$1" pin="2" pad="2"/></connects>
<technologies><technology name=""/></technologies>
</device></devices>
</deviceset>
tools.notes: Gate addlevel is must | can | next | request | always; connect route="any" allows several pads per pin. Managed-library objects carry urn, library_version and locally_modified attributes.

tools.name: <schematic> (XML)
tools.description: Schematic content with xreflabel/xrefpart format attributes: <libraries>, <attributes> (global), <variantdefs>, <classes>, <modules>, <groups>, <parts>/<part> (name, library, deviceset, device, technology, value, attributes, variants), <sheets>/<sheet> and <errors> (approved ERC messages). Each sheet holds <plain>, <moduleinsts>, <instances>/<instance part gate x y rot>, <busses> and <nets>/<net name class> whose <segment>s contain wires, <pinref part gate pin>, <portref>, <junction>, <label> and <probe>.
tools.usage: <!ELEMENT schematic (description?, libraries?, attributes?, variantdefs?, classes?, modules?, groups?, parts?, sheets?, errors?)>
tools.example:
<parts><part name="R1" library="ngspice-simulation" deviceset="R" device="" value="1k"/></parts>
<sheets><sheet>
<instances><instance part="R1" gate="G$1" x="30.48" y="40.64"/></instances>
<nets><net name="VCAP1" class="0"><segment>
<wire x1="43.18" y1="40.64" x2="50.8" y2="40.64" width="0.1524" layer="91"/>
<pinref part="R1" gate="G$1" pin="2"/>
</segment></net></nets>
</sheet></sheets>
tools.notes: A netlist can be read directly from <pinref> elements per <net>; nets with the same name on different sheets are one net.

tools.name: <board> (XML)
tools.description: Board content: <plain> (outline, texts, holes, splines), <libraries>, <attributes>, <variantdefs>, <classes>/<class> with <clearance>, <designrules> with <param name value> (the .dru parameters), <autorouter> with <pass>/<param> and <groups>. Placed parts are <elements>/<element> (name, library, package, value, x, y, rot, locked, populate, smashed, attributes), and connectivity is in <signals>/<signal name class> with <contactref element pad>, <wire>, <via> and <polygon>. Manufacturing preview colours and <errors> (approved DRC messages) close the section.
tools.usage: <!ELEMENT board (description?, fusionsync?, fusionteam?, plain?, libraries?, attributes?, variantdefs?, classes?, designrules?, autorouter?, groups?, elements?, signals?, mfgpreviewcolors?, errors?)>
tools.example:
<classes><class number="1" name="power" width="0.4" drill="0.6"/></classes>
<elements><element name="C4" library="rcl" package="TAP5-45" value="47u/25V" x="4.445" y="6.985" smashed="yes" rot="R180"/></elements>
<signals><signal name="GND" class="1">
<contactref element="C4" pad="-"/>
<wire x1="4.4" y1="4.4" x2="10" y2="4.4" width="0.4" layer="16"/>
<via x="10" y="4.4" extent="1-16" drill="0.6"/>
</signal></signals>
tools.notes: Via and airwire 'extent' is 'topmost-bottommost' layer, e.g. 1-16; fusionsync/fusionteam hold links to Fusion documents.

tools.name: Drawing primitives (XML)
tools.description: The graphic and copper objects shared by all drawing types: <wire> (x1 y1 x2 y2 width layer, optional curve, style, cap), <polygon> with <vertex> points (width, layer, spacing, pour solid|hatch|cutout, isolate, orphans, thermals, rank), <via>, <pad> (drill, diameter, shape square|round|octagon|long|offset, stop, thermals, first), <smd> (dx, dy, roundness, stop, thermals, cream), <text>, <circle>, <rectangle>, <hole>, <dimension>, <frame>, <spline> and <attribute>. All coordinates and sizes are in millimetres.
tools.usage: See eagle.dtd section 'Basic objects'
tools.example:
<pad name="1" x="-1.27" y="0" drill="0.8" shape="octagon"/>
<smd name="2" x="0.75" y="0" dx="0.9" dy="1" layer="1" roundness="25"/>
<polygon width="0.3" layer="16" isolate="0.3" rank="1"><vertex x="0" y="0"/><vertex x="50" y="0"/><vertex x="50" y="40"/></polygon>
<text x="0" y="2" size="1.27" layer="25">>NAME</text>
tools.notes: Polygon rank is 1..6 in signals and 0 or 7 in packages; wire curve ranges -359.9..359.9 degrees; text font is vector | proportional | fixed.

tools.name: Modules, variants and groups (XML)
tools.description: Elements for hierarchy, assembly variants and persistent groups. <module name prefix dx dy> contains <ports>/<port name side coord direction>, its own parts and sheets; <moduleinst name module x y> places it on a sheet and <portref moduleinst port> connects nets to its ports. <variantdefs>/<variantdef name current> declare assembly variants, <variant name populate value technology> overrides a part or element, and <schematic_group>/<board_group> define groups that objects reference via grouprefs.
tools.usage: <module> in <modules>; <moduleinst> in <sheet><moduleinsts>; <variantdef> in <variantdefs>; <variant> inside <part>/<element>
tools.example:
<variantdefs><variantdef name="lowCost" current="yes"/></variantdefs>
<part name="R7" library="rcl" deviceset="R-EU_" device="R0603" value="10k">
<variant name="lowCost" populate="no"/>
</part>
<moduleinst name="PSU1" module="PWR" x="50.8" y="25.4"/>
tools.notes: Variants in <element> are accepted only for compatibility with EAGLE 6.x files; the CAM Processor selects a variant with -A.
